item.title: Billboard’s 2026 Top Music Lawyers Revealed
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's episode of "Trending on Billboard". Today, we're diving into the world of music and copyright law, where the rise of generative artificial intelligence is changing the game.
[Soft music transitions in the background]
Host: The US Constitution grants Congress the power to promote the progress of science and useful arts, which includes protecting creators' work through copyright. But what happens when AI tools use massive amounts of copyrighted data to generate new music? Some call it transformational technology, while others see it as digital theft.
[Pause for emphasis]
Host: The issue has consumed the legal community, with top music lawyers guiding superstars and industry-driving companies through the complex landscape. According to J. Douglas Baldridge, a partner at Venable, "artificial intelligence continues to present the most important legal issues facing the music industry".
[Short music transition]
Host: Just two years ago, major music groups like Universal, Sony, and Warner Music Group sued AI companies Suno and Udio, alleging they unlawfully copied songs to train their models. The AI companies argue that copyright law's fair use doctrine protects their actions, but musicians and labels disagree.
[Soft music continues]
Host: Recently, Warner Music Group and Universal have struck licensing deals with Suno and Udio to settle their suits. However, Sony and Universal are still in court against these AI companies. The music industry is trying to avoid past mistakes and is seeking partnerships to license AI content with limits on its use.
[Closing music starts playing]
Host: The National Music Publishers' Association has announced licensing deals with Udio and KLAY, another AI company. But some music creators are urging caution, as the debate continues to unfold. That's all for today's episode. Thanks for tuning in to "Trending on Billboard".
[Outro music plays]
